newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: INDO AND AUSTRALIA CONCLUDE AGREEMENT

Indonesia's Foreign Minister Ali Alatas and Australia's Foreign Minister Alexander Downer, have formally concluded 25 years of negotiations by signing a Maritime Boundary Agreement at a ceremony in Perth.
The agreement covers boundaries stretching three thousand kilometres from Java to the Gulf of Carpentaria and between Java and Christmas Island.
It sets out seabed boundaries and exclusive economic zones. A small group of unionists held a protest outside the signing ceremony demanding Indonesia release trade union officials from jail.
The protestors claim the Indonesian union officials have been imprisoned for simply doing their jobs.
WILLIAMS TELLS STATES MONEY FOR LEGAL AID IS ALL THERE IS
Federal Attorney General Daryl Williams says he's told the States the same money allocated in the budget for legal aid is all that's available.
A meeting of Attorneys General in Melbourne, has been discussing the legal aid crisis with Mr Williams.
Mr Williams says the Northern Territory today has reached an agreement, to maintain its current funding level, while agreement is close for Queensland.
The Victorian Attorney General Jan Wade says she's received a better offer, but it's still not good enough.
MINCHIN REPAYING TRAVEL ALLOWANCE
Parliamentary Secretary to the Prime Minister, Nick Minchin, says he's repaying more than three thousand dollars in travel allowance paid to him during last year's election campaign.
Senator Minchin travelled with the Opposition leader and was paid travel allowance by the Department of the Senate in accordance with the rules.
He says he understood at the time, that if he was travelling with the Opposition leader and undertaking duties as his Parliamentary Secretary, he was entitled to claim travel allowance.

Senator Minchin says it's been drawn to his attention the convention is no shadow ministers claimed travel allowance from the time of the Liberal Campaign launch to the election, so he's sent a cheque to the Government for the three-thousand-150 dollars paid to him.
PANELS TO GUIDE ON FILM CENSORSHIP
Independent panels of citizens, which will view films before they're released, will soon be involved in the classification of films and videos.
The plan to use 20-member panels, to reflect community attitudes, was endorsed today by all Australian governments at a meeting of Attorneys-General in Melbourne.
The Chief Censor, John Dickie, says he doesn't expect the move will lead to tighter restrictions on movies, and says the panels won't have the right of veto over the censor.
He says they'll be purely advisory panels.
WOMAN APPOINTED AS CHIEF MEDICAL OFFICER IN FIRST
The Commonwealth Health Department has appointed its first woman Chief Medical Officer Professor Judith Whitworth, who's Professor of Medicine at Sydney's St George Hospital.
Health Department Secretary, Andrew Podger, says Professor Whitworth has an outstanding reputation as a researcher and clinician in the area of renal medicine.
Mr Podger says she was also the first woman to be appointed to chair the Medical Research Committee of the National Health and Medical Research Council.
UNION SAYS YOUNG DOCTOR INVESTMENT LOST

The union representing junior doctors in their dispute over Medicare provider numbers, says taxpayers spend a "small fortune" training doctors, and that investment will now be lost. Junior doctors have voted to continue their strike until next Friday because the Federal Government is restricting provider numbers needed for young graduates wanting to go into general practice.
The Public Service Association President, Maurie O'Sullivan, says Health Minister Michael Wooldridge must reverse his decision.
But Doctor Wooldridge says the decision by young doctors is not the Government's fault.
He's described young doctors as a very priveleged group of young people, who are seeking a guarantee of a job other people in the community don't have.
MEETING AGREES TO FREE EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION
A meeting today of Australia's Education Ministers in Melbourne has agreed to a free exchange of information between the states on paedophile teachers.
A task force will be set up to organise the scheme.
The New South Wales Education Minister, John Aquilina, who pushed for the agreement, says he's delighted, because it's in the interests of Australia's children.
But the Australian Education Union says the ministers have failed to see the benefit of a licencing system in the interests of students and parents.
GOLF WRAP - HONDA CLASSIC AND LPGA WOMENS
Australian Stuart Appleby is in a group of 5 players tied for second at 4 under, and just one shot off the pace after one round of the Honda Golf Classic in Florida.
Wayne Grady fired a one over 73, Craig Parry a two over 74. At the LPGA event in Tucson, Arizona, Sweden's Liselotte Neumann is a one shot leader after firing a first round 8 under 64.
Australian's Jan Stephenson and Jane Geddes are 3 under, Britain's Laura Davies 2 under while Karrie Webb shot a first round 71 to be one under.
And Peter O'Malley will take a one shot lead into tonight's second round of the Portugese Open.
